# ============================================================
# Population Growth and CO2 Emissions - all figures for the report
# Output files match the names expected by Population_CO2_Report.tex
# Put the two CSV files in the working directory (or edit the paths).
# ============================================================

pkgs <- c("ggplot2", "dplyr", "tidyr", "scales", "reshape2")
for (p in pkgs) if (!requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)) install.packages(p)
library(ggplot2); library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(scales); library(reshape2)

# ---------- 1. Import ----------
pop <- read.csv("C:\\Users\\100060\\OneDrive - AIF Rwanda\\Isimbi, Ines\\Downloads\\world_population.csv", check.names = TRUE)
co2 <- read.csv("C:\Users\\100060\\OneDrive - AIF Rwanda\\Isimbi, Ines\\Downloads\\CO2_emission.csv", check.names = TRUE)

# ---------- 2. Cleaning ----------
pop <- unique(pop)
co2 <- unique(co2)
# drop the duplicated 2019 column only if identical
if ("X2019.1" %in% names(co2) &&
    isTRUE(all.equal(co2$X2019, co2$X2019.1))) co2$X2019.1 <- NULL

year_cols <- paste0("X", 1990:2019)

# Fill only short INTERNAL gaps (<= 2 consecutive NAs) by linear interpolation
fill_short_gaps <- function(v, max_gap = 2) {
  n <- length(v); i <- 1
  while (i <= n) {
    if (is.na(v[i])) {
      j <- i
      while (j <= n && is.na(v[j])) j <- j + 1
      if (i > 1 && j <= n && (j - i) <= max_gap) {
        v[i:(j - 1)] <- approx(c(i - 1, j), c(v[i - 1], v[j]), xout = i:(j - 1))$y
      }
      i <- j
    } else i <- i + 1
  }
  v
}
co2_i <- co2
co2_i[year_cols] <- t(apply(co2[year_cols], 1, fill_short_gaps))

# ---------- 3. Merge ----------
m  <- left_join(pop, co2[,   c("country_code", year_cols)], by = c("CCA3" = "country_code"))
mi <- left_join(pop, co2_i[, c("country_code", year_cols)], by = c("CCA3" = "country_code"))

# ---------- 4. Top 10 ----------
top10 <- pop %>% arrange(desc(X2022.Population)) %>% slice(1:10)

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
            theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
                  legend.position = "right"))

# ---------- Fig 1: top10_bar.png ----------
p1 <- ggplot(top10, aes(x = reorder(Country.Territory, X2022.Population),
                        y = X2022.Population / 1e6)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2a6f97") +
  geom_text(aes(label = comma(round(X2022.Population / 1e6))), hjust = -0.1, size = 3) +
  coord_flip() + expand_limits(y = 1700) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Population 2022 (millions)")
ggsave("top10_bar.png", p1, width = 6, height = 4.2, dpi = 200)

# ---------- Fig 2: trend_population.png ----------
pop_long <- top10 %>%
  select(Country.Territory, X1990.Population, X2000.Population, X2010.Population,
         X2015.Population, X2020.Population, X2022.Population) %>%
  pivot_longer(-Country.Territory, names_to = "Year", values_to = "Population") %>%
  mutate(Year = as.numeric(gsub("X|\\.Population", "", Year)))
p2 <- ggplot(pop_long, aes(Year, Population / 1e6, colour = Country.Territory)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) + geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1990, 2000, 2010, 2015, 2020, 2022)) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Population (millions)", colour = NULL)
ggsave("trend_population.png", p2, width = 6, height = 4.2, dpi = 200)

# ---------- Fig 3: co2_trend.png (interpolated series, gaps stay NA) ----------
co2_top <- mi %>% filter(CCA3 %in% top10$CCA3) %>%
  select(Country.Territory, all_of(year_cols)) %>%
  pivot_longer(-Country.Territory, names_to = "Year", values_to = "CO2") %>%
  mutate(Year = as.numeric(sub("X", "", Year)))
p3 <- ggplot(co2_top, aes(Year, CO2, colour = Country.Territory)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8, na.rm = TRUE) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = expression(CO[2]~"per person (t)"), colour = NULL)
ggsave("co2_trend.png", p3, width = 6, height = 4.2, dpi = 200)

# ---------- Fig 4: corr_heatmap.png ----------
cm <- cor(pop[, c("Area..km..", "Density..per.km..", "Growth.Rate",
                  "World.Population.Percentage")], use = "complete.obs")
colnames(cm) <- rownames(cm) <- c("Area", "Density", "Growth rate", "World %")
cm_long <- melt(cm)
p4 <- ggplot(cm_long, aes(Var1, Var2, fill = value)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", value)), size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#b2182b", mid = "white", high = "#2166ac",
                       midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "r") + coord_fixed()
ggsave("corr_heatmap.png", p4, width = 4.6, height = 4, dpi = 200)

# ---------- Fig 5: scatter_pop_co2pc.png + regression ----------
d <- m %>% filter(!is.na(X2022.Population), !is.na(X2019))
fit <- lm(X2019 ~ X2022.Population, data = d)
print(summary(fit))
cat("Pearson :"); print(cor.test(d$X2022.Population, d$X2019, method = "pearson"))
cat("Spearman:"); print(cor.test(d$X2022.Population, d$X2019, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE))

lab <- d %>% filter(Country.Territory %in% c("China", "India", "United States", "Qatar", "Indonesia"))
p5 <- ggplot(d, aes(X2022.Population / 1e6, X2019)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, colour = "#2a6f97") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, colour = "crimson") +
  geom_text(data = lab, aes(label = Country.Territory), size = 2.8,
            hjust = -0.1, vjust = -0.5) +
  labs(x = "Population 2022 (millions)", y = expression(CO[2]~"per person 2019 (t)"))
ggsave("scatter_pop_co2pc.png", p5, width = 6.2, height = 4.2, dpi = 200)

# ---------- Fig 6: diagnostics.png (residuals vs fitted + Q-Q) ----------
png("diagnostics.png", width = 7, height = 3.2, units = "in", res = 200)
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 1, 1))
plot(fitted(fit), resid(fit), pch = 16, cex = 0.6, col = "#2a6f97",
     xlab = "Fitted", ylab = "Residuals"); abline(h = 0, col = "crimson")
qqnorm(resid(fit), main = "", pch = 16, cex = 0.6, col = "#2a6f97"); qqline(resid(fit), col = "crimson")
dev.off()

# ---------- Fig 7: boxplots.png ----------
png("boxplots.png", width = 7, height = 3.2, units = "in", res = 200)
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 2, 1, 1))
boxplot(pop$X2022.Population / 1e6, horizontal = TRUE, xlab = "Population 2022 (millions)")
boxplot(co2$X2019, horizontal = TRUE, xlab = expression(CO[2]~"per person 2019 (t)"))
dev.off()

# ---------- Fig 8: continent_co2.png ----------
cont <- d %>% group_by(Continent) %>%
  summarise(Sum = sum(X2019), Mean = mean(X2019), N = n()) %>% arrange(desc(Sum))
print(cont)
p8 <- ggplot(cont, aes(reorder(Continent, -Sum), Sum)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2a6f97") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = expression("Sum of country-level"~CO[2]~"per person (t)")) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 25, hjust = 1))
ggsave("continent_co2.png", p8, width = 6, height = 3.8, dpi = 200)

cat("\nAll figures saved in:", getwd(), "\n")
